plan.title: engine:invoke falls back to global deft for runtime verbs; _ts-build resolves pnpm via Corepack

narratives.Description: engine:invoke currently fail-closes when packages/cli/dist/bin.js is missing on a buildable source tree, even if a working global deft is on PATH. Separately, engine:_ts-build and tasks/ts.yml hardcode bare pnpm, so machines with Node/Corepack but no pnpm on PATH fail with exit 127. This story fixes both in tasks/engine.yml (and ts.yml): allowlist runtime/session verbs for global fallback with a skew warning, and resolve the pinned packageManager via Corepack without reintroducing auto-build on session verbs (#2181).
narratives.Overview:
## Summary

Two related adoption-blockers in `tasks/engine.yml` on unbuilt framework source checkouts:

1. **#2409** — `engine:invoke` fail-closes when `packages/cli/dist/bin.js` is missing on a buildable source tree, even when a working global `deft` is on PATH. Session/runtime verbs (`session:start`, `verify:session-ritual`, `verify:tools`, `triage:summary`, `triage:welcome`, `verify:cache-fresh`) should prefer local dist, then fall back to global with a skew warning — without reintroducing auto-`pnpm build` (#2181).
2. **#2410** — `engine:_ts-build` (and `tasks/ts.yml`) hardcode bare `pnpm`. Machines with Node/Corepack but no `pnpm` on PATH fail with exit 127. Resolve the pinned manager via Corepack (`package.json#packageManager`); optional `DEFT_PACKAGE_MANAGER=npm`; actionable remediation when neither works.

## Acceptance

- Unbuilt source + global `deft` → `task session:start` (and other #2181 runtime verbs) succeed without pnpm/build
- Build-gated verbs may still fail-closed or require `task build`
- Unbuilt source + Corepack, no bare pnpm → `task build` / `_ts-build` works via Corepack pin
- Clear error when neither pnpm nor Corepack can satisfy the pin
- Contract/tests cover both paths; #2181 no-auto-build invariant preserved

Refs #2181, #2142, #2120 (closed).
narratives.ImplementationPlan: 1. tasks/engine.yml `invoke`: when dist missing on buildable source, if `command -v deft` (or directive) succeeds, invoke global with a one-line skew warning (global version vs package.json pin) for an allowlist of runtime/session verbs; keep fail-closed for build-gated verbs; optional DEFT_USE_GLOBAL_CLI=1 force. Do NOT call pnpm/build. 2. tasks/engine.yml `_ts-build` + tasks/ts.yml: when bare pnpm missing, invoke via Corepack using package.json packageManager pin (e.g. corepack pnpm@<pin> --dir … run build); honor DEFT_PACKAGE_MANAGER=npm as explicit secondary; fail with remediation naming Corepack/packageManager. 3. Align doctor/toolchain messaging. 4. Tests/contracts: unbuilt+global runtime success; bare-pnpm-missing+Corepack-present build success; #2181 no-auto-build on session:start.
narratives.UserStory: As a maintainer on an unbuilt framework source checkout, I want session/runtime tasks to use a global deft when dist is missing and builds to resolve pnpm via Corepack, so that adoption is not blocked by a missing local build or bare pnpm on PATH.

items.title: Runtime verbs fall back to global deft without building

narrative.Acceptance: Given an unbuilt source checkout with global deft on PATH, when `task session:start` (or another #2181 runtime/session verb) runs, then it exits 0 without invoking pnpm/npm/build and may print a skew warning.

items.title: Missing dist and no global still fail-closes

narrative.Acceptance: Given an unbuilt source checkout with no global deft, when a runtime verb is invoked, then engine:invoke fail-closes with actionable install/build remediation.
Given Node+Corepack and no pnpm on PATH, when `task build` / `_ts-build` runs, then it succeeds via the package.json packageManager pin (or DEFT_PACKAGE_MANAGER=npm when explicitly set).

items.title: Actionable error when neither pnpm nor Corepack works

narrative.Acceptance: Given neither bare pnpm nor Corepack can satisfy the pin, when build runs, then the error names Corepack/packageManager remediation clearly.
Given the content-contract tests for runtime session and engine dispatch, when they run, then they cover global-fallback and Corepack paths and still assert session:start does not auto-build.
